principles.text: Design the product backward from distribution: build something that goes viral and explains itself on camera in seconds.
Win organic on volume: one creator per brand account, many accounts, cut low performers and double down on winners.
Pay creators a small retainer plus about 20% of the sales they generate, so their pay tracks performance.
The viral video brings eyeballs; the comment-reply videos that sell hard drive most of the conversions.
In B2B, tie every message to dollars lost and recovered, and price with a performance tier customers grow into a retainer.

sampleQA.question: How should I structure creator deals for organic TikTok?

answer.text: Pay a small retainer, about $500 to $1,000 a month, plus 20% of the revenue each creator drives.
Give each creator their own brand account and scale horizontally; stacking creators on one page confuses the algorithm.
Hand them past winning concepts instead of scripts, because what goes viral once will go viral again.
Cut low performers and double down on the creators pushing views.

sampleQA.question: How should I price a B2B service so clients don't churn?

answer.text: High retainers made clients hypersensitive to results; a performance-based downsell converted far better.
Pure pay-per-result drew tire kickers, so he added a small monitoring fee to filter for committed buyers.
Customers who outgrow the performance tier opt into the unlimited retainer on their own.
Don't give the product away free: paying customers have skin in the game and give real feedback.

sampleQA.question: Someone is copying my product. What do I do first?

answer.text: Register trademarks and copyrights and keep dated records so you can prove ownership.
Prefer platform takedowns over lawsuits when the goal is fast removal; litigation is slow, costly and uncertain.
Go after the infrastructure supporting the bad actor: domain, registrar, host and payment processor.
Keep serving customers and shipping faster; time spent obsessing over imitators erodes your advantage.
